proposals.reason: English personal name yiyin is left uncapitalized; standardize to Yi Yin.
Uncapitalized yiyin; 名 marks an alternate name rather than a style name.

proposals.before: Wuxian brought order to the royal house and composed Salted Mugwort and Taiwu.
proposals.after: Wuxian brought order to the royal house and composed Xian Ai and Taiwu.
proposals.reason: 咸艾 is a document title, not the foods 'salted mugwort'.

proposals.before: He named Western Earl Chang, the Nine Marquises, and the Marquis of E as the three high dukes.
proposals.after: He named Western Earl Chang, the Marquis of Jiu, and the Marquis of E as the three high dukes.
proposals.reason: 九侯 is a singular lordly title, not a plural 'Nine Marquises'.

proposals.before: The Marquis of E disputed it strongly, argued it swiftly; together he pickled the Marquis of E.
proposals.after: The Marquis of E disputed it strongly and argued it swiftly; [Zhou] also pickled the Marquis of E.
proposals.reason: Subject of 脯 is Zhou, not the Marquis himself; literal English wrongly makes him the agent.

decisions.reason: Focus unit 伊尹曰 names 伊尹; uncapitalized English “yiyin” is an orthographic error, and “Yi Yin” correctly renders the personal name while leaving the rest of the sentence unchanged.
伊尹名阿衡 uses 名 (“was named”), not a style-name formula such as 字; capitalizing Yi Yin and replacing “styled” with “named” both match the Chinese.
作咸艾，作太戊 is the parallel document-composition formula (cf. 作原命 in s0107); “Salted Mugwort” invents a food sense for the title 咸艾, and “Xian Ai” correctly treats it as a work title.

以西伯昌、九侯、鄂侯為三公 lists three singular lords as the three dukes; 九侯 is one titled individual parallel to 鄂侯, not a plural “Nine Marquises,” as the following units’ daughter and execution narrative confirm.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以西伯昌、九侯、鄂侯為三公

decisions.after: The Marquis of E disputed it strongly and argued it swiftly; Zhou also pickled the Marquis of E.
decisions.reason: Continuing from 紂怒……醢九侯, 并脯鄂侯 has Zhou as the agent of 脯 and 并 as “also”; the before wrongly makes the Marquis pickle himself. The proposal’s agent fix is right, but bracketed “[Zhou]” is editorial markup, so the revised literal names Zhou in natural English.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English “yiyin” was created only by the uncapitalized mistranslation of 伊尹; the Chinese supports the correct personal name already recorded as Yi Yin (c0065), not a separate “yiyin” name.
Accepted r0004 shows English “Nine Marquises” was created only by misreading singular 九侯 as a plural; the Chinese supports the singular title Marquis of Jiu (c0240), not a separate plural name.
